A balcony solar generator is a compact solar power system designed for apartments, condos, and homes with limited outdoor space.

There are two main types:

Type

	

How it works

Plug-in balcony solar

The important distinction is that a battery-based solar generator generally does not reduce your home's overall electricity consumption from the grid unless you deliberately power appliances from it.

A balcony solar generator is a compact solar power system designed for apartments, condos, and homes with limited outdoor space.

It typically combines solar panels with an inverter and, optionally, a battery to generate electricity from sunlight.

There are two main types:

Type

	

How it works

	

Best for




Plug-in balcony solar

	

Solar panels and a microinverter feed electricity into your home's electrical system

	

Reducing electricity bills




Solar generator with battery

	

Solar panels charge a portable battery that powers appliances

	

Backup power, portable use

A typical system uses 400–800 watts of solar panels. Actual energy production depends on sunlight, panel orientation, shading, and installation.

Important for the US: Plug-in balcony solar systems face electrical-code, utility-interconnection, and equipment-approval requirements. You should not assume a system can safely or legally be connected to an ordinary wall outlet.

In California, a new plug-in solar law is scheduled to take effect on January 1, 2027, covering qualifying systems up to 1,200 W. Equipment certification and installation requirements still matter.
